text:
Minnesota built a 3-0 lead before the second period was ten minutes old and then held on for a 4-2 win in Philadelphia, a game the Flyers probably should have won on the way they played it. Our numbers give PHI a 61% chance to win if the same shots were replayed over and over, and the shot attempts were 64 to 51 in their favor. Expected goals (a measure of chance quality) ran 3.28 to 2.63 for PHI.

The gap came down to the crease and to who cashed in early. Matt Boldy, drafted 12th overall in 2019 and a point-a-game college player at Boston College, scored at 4:06 of the first and added an assist on Joel Eriksson Ek's goal at the start of the second. Michael McCarron made it 2-0 31 seconds after Boldy. Jesper Wallstedt faced shots worth 3.28 expected goals and allowed two, which our model scores as 1.28 goals saved above expected. Dan Vladar gave up three on shots worth 2.63.

Philadelphia pushed back late. Tyson Foerster tipped one in at 14:24 of the second, and Denver Barkey, the 95th pick in 2023, scored on the power play early in the third to make it 3-2. The Flyers out-chanced MIN 1.21 to 0.56 in expected goals in that period, but Danila Yurov sealed it at 18:36 on a shot our model gave a chance of under 1%. That leaves MIN with a road win built on early finishing and a hot goalie, and PHI with a loss its underlying numbers say it didn't earn.
